## How this repository is being worked

Changes go through the [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md) workflow end to end: branch, implement, ui-review, verifier, code-review, PR. PRs merge when CI is green. Findings become issues. The loop continues to the next item without pausing for step-by-step approval.

The point is that it runs unattended, so stopping to confirm each step defeats it.

## What still gets surfaced rather than decided silently

Proceeding by default does not mean deciding everything. Three categories get a recommendation and a question:

1. **Changes to what users see** — image quality, layout tradeoffs. #96 is the live example: re-encoding to WebP is well-measured, but q82/600px is a judgment about acceptable fidelity, not a fact.
2. **Changes to other contributors' behavior** — #147 committed tool config that runs hooks on anyone's machine who clones. That deserved saying out loud, not just doing.
3. **Rewrites of shared history** — never silently. See the note below on why this keeps coming up.

The rest of the work does not wait on those answers. Finish everything that does not depend on the decision first, then ask.

## Two things that have repeatedly caught people out

**Checks that run without asserting on what they produced.** This is the repo's signature defect, found three separate times: the E2E smoke passed against a chat service returning `fallback: true`; the seed ran green on every PR while writing credentials that could never authenticate (#141); a category page referenced an image that had never existed (#137). A green check is not evidence unless something inspects its output.

**Verifying in a richer environment than the real one.** Also recurring: a populated local venv vs CI's bare one; jsdom vs a real browser; three sampled viewports vs the breakpoint boundaries where the defects actually live; `node_modules` vs the standalone image; a local stack reading `.env` vs CI with none. If a check passes locally, confirm it runs in the environment that matters.

**Deleting files does not shrink `git clone`.** The blobs stay reachable from history. #146 removed 68.6 MB from the working tree and the web image; `size-pack` did not move. Worth remembering before promising a clone-size win — see the measurement in #66.

## Running the stack locally

Environments differ per machine (port collisions, whether Ollama is installed for `LLM_PROVIDER=local`). `make e2e-smoke` may need a compose override for ports and provider. Resolve collisions with an override file using `ports: !override` — a plain `ports:` list appends rather than replaces — and never by stopping containers you did not start.

## Current state

`main` is clean. #145, #146 and #147 are merged. **Verifying in a richer environment than the real one.** Also recurring: a populated local venv vs CI's bare one; jsdom vs a real browser; three sampled viewports vs the breakpoint boundaries where the defects actually live; `node_modules` vs the standalone image; a local stack reading `.env` vs CI with none. If a check passes locally, confirm it runs in the environment that matters.

**Deleting files does not shrink `git clone`.** The blobs stay reachable from history. #146 removed 68.6 MB from the working tree and the web image; `size-pack` did not move. Worth remembering before promising a clone-size win — see the measurement in #66.

## Running the stack locally

Environments differ per machine (port collisions, whether Ollama is installed for `LLM_PROVIDER=local`). `make e2e-smoke` may need a compose override for ports and provider. Resolve collisions with an override file using `ports: !override` — a plain `ports:` list appends rather than replaces — and never by stopping containers you did not start.

## Current state

`main` is clean. #145, #146 and #147 are merged. {"assignees":[],"body":"Found while running `make -C apps/web ci` on a comment-only branch, which failed. The same suite passed on the next run with nothing changed, which is the part worth writing down: this repository's `playwright.config.ts` says "Retries are off. A retried failure is a failure that gets ignored, and a suite nobody trusts is the state this repo has been recovering from." The vitest suite has no such protection and this is the failure mode it exists to prevent.

## Measured

```
$ make -C apps/web ci
 Test Files  2 failed | 35 passed (37)
      Tests  2 failed | 155 passed (157)

$ npx vitest run          # nothing changed
 Test Files  37 passed (37)
      Tests  157 passed (157)
```

Then, across six consecutive full-suite runs on the same tree:

```
run 1  FAIL  src/app/page.test.tsx > Home page > names a product card once   (8640ms)
run 2  pass
run 3  FAIL  src/app/page.test.tsx > Home page > names a product card once   (5280ms)
runs 4-9  pass
```

In isolation it never fails — `npx vitest run src/app/page.test.tsx` passed 4/4.

## It is a timeout, not a wrong assertion

The failure is reported at `src/app/page.test.tsx:21`, which is the `it(...)` declaration, not `:33` where the `expect` is. Both failing runs exceeded vitest's default 5000ms test timeout: 8640ms and 5280ms. The passing runs complete the whole file in a fraction of that.

The correlation is with machine load rather than with anything in the test. The failing full-suite run reported `environment 350.65s` against `154.06s` for a passing one on the same tree — roughly double the jsdom setup cost across the suite.

## Why this test in particular

`src/app/page.test.tsx` renders the entire home page: `render(await Home())`, with only `header` and `block` mocked. `Home()` reads the real `public/categories.json` and the page renders every category and product card in it — the largest DOM any test in this suite builds. `getByRole('link', { name })` then computes accessible names across that tree. So it has the least headroom against a fixed 5s budget, and it is the first to cross it when the machine is busy.

Nothing here is non-deterministic in *content* — both the test and the component read the same file from disk, no database, no network. It is purely a time budget.

## Not fully captured

The original `make ci` failure reported **2** failed files; I only identified this one before the suite went green again. The second was not recorded. Whatever it was, it is likely the same mechanism — the next-largest render in the suite.

## Worth deciding

- Whether the fix is a longer `testTimeout` for this file (or suite-wide in `vitest.config.ts`), or making the test render less than the whole catalogue.
- Raising the timeout hides the signal that this test is slow; rendering less weakens what it covers. The test's own comment explains that it deliberately runs against the real `public/categories.json` because "the category page's equivalent test mocks its data source, so the two together cover the same property from both directions" — so trimming it is not free.
- CI has passed consistently so far, so this is currently a local-machine problem. That is not a reason to leave it: a GitHub runner under a noisy neighbour has the same fixed 5s budget, and the failure would land on an unrelated pull request.
","labels":[],"number":283,"state":"OPEN","title":"page.test.tsx flakes on a 5s timeout under load, and the vitest suite has no flake policy"}

==================== 2026-08-05T14:43:21Z
Session update. #96 is done (#152); `main` is at 28d4492 and clean.

## What changed in the repository

`apps/web/public/images` 534 MiB → **156.2 MiB**; web image ~1.15 GB → **693 MB** against a 1.5 GB budget. 852 catalogue images re-encoded to WebP at q90, keeping the originals' 1024×1024.

Also landed: the e2e image check now sees `/_next/image` requests (it was watching three CSS backgrounds and none of the 852 catalogue images), and the category grid's `sizes` matches its actual 397px box.

## Additions to the two recurring traps this issue names

**"Checks that run without asserting on what they produced" has a sibling: checks whose documentation claims more than they assert.** Four review rounds on #152, and after the first real defect every subsequent finding was a comment overstating a guard — not the guard itself. Once the numbers were right, the *rationale* was still wrong: I justified a mean-weight ceiling by the lossless case, but the per-file ceiling fails on a single offender and lossless puts most files over it, so that scenario was already covered and the second ceiling's real job (a quality bump that stays under the per-file limit) was written down nowhere.

The q

==================== 2026-08-05T15:28:18Z
The "findings become issues" practice this issue records is now in the runbook itself, as *Unrelated findings become issues* in AGENTS.md (#155).

It had been living only here. That worked while this issue was the handover document, but it meant anyone reading AGENTS.md to learn how the repository is worked would not find it — and it is a rule about what to do mid-change, which is exactly where the runbook is being read.

**This issue keeps the durable session context; AGENTS.md now holds the rule.** Worth keeping that split in mind for anything else recorded here that is really a standing instruction rather than context.

## What the rule adds beyond what was written here

- File **at the moment of finding**, before deciding what to do about it.
- The two failure modes it sits between: silently widening a reviewed diff, and silently dropping the finding into a chat reply.
- A narrow exception for fixing in place — a pre-existing problem the change makes materially worse, or a check that has to work for the change to be verifiable — with the reason required in the commit message. Both cases occurred in #152.
- Sub-agents report; the main agent files.

## Two corrections during its 

==================== 2026-08-05T16:54:34Z
#150 done in #159. `main` at f3fe471, clean. That closes every loose thread the #96 re-encode left behind.

## The lesson from this one is the recurring trap, in a new place

`next.config.js` now derives its srcset ceiling from `config/catalogue_images.json`, which meant it had to `require` a file above `apps/web/`. **The Dockerfile's builder stage copies individual files out of `apps/web/`, so the image build failed with `Cannot find module`** — and would have taken down `docker/build-push-action` and both e2e-smoke jobs — while `quick-ci`, a local `next build`, and all 142 script tests passed.

Caught by `ui-review`, and only because it builds the image in order to render against it. Nothing in the local loop could have seen it: the working tree has the file, the build context does not.

Worth generalising, because the shape recurs: **a config file that reaches outside its own package is a build-context question, not just a path question.** Anything added under `config/` that a surface reads at build time needs the corresponding `COPY`, and the local build will never tell you.

## What the rendered pass was worth

`ui-review` built a second server from `main`'s config and diffed 

==================== 2026-08-05T17:53:48Z
The three workflow adjustments are in `main` (#161, at 8032d65). Recording what they are and, more usefully, what their own review round said about them.

## What changed

- **Step 4** — the red phase does not reach a guard added for behaviour that already works. Requires the mistake-to-assertion mapping written down and demonstrated, including the mistakes nothing catches, and names how to point a guard at a fixture without damaging the checkout.
- **Step 6** — a viewport is a width in CSS pixels. Where a change affects what the browser requests, exercise 2× as well as 1×.
- **Step 8** — the reviewer classifies findings as defects or refinements; the loop ends on a round with no defects. Step 10 exempts refinements it already cleared, or it re-arms the loop step 8 just closed.

`.claude/agents/ui-review.md` and `code-review.md` moved with it. Two of the three would otherwise have required behaviour the agents performing those steps were never told about — `ui-review` had no concept of density and no mechanism for it, `code-review` had no defect/refinement vocabulary.

## The pattern this session ends on

Six documentation defects across #152, #155 and #161, every one caught by rev

==================== 2026-08-07T06:01:17Z
Session update. Four image-delivery fixes merged: #163, #167, #172, #175. `main` at 0b2e8f1, clean.

## What landed

Two halves of one question — how a change to a sub-agent definition gets validated — landing in the same `AGENTS.md` section, so one change rather than two conflicting edits to the same paragraphs.

## #285: I filed it wrong, then corrected it wrong

The issue claimed definitions are read once at session start. I "corrected" that to say an agent receives what is committed in `HEAD`. **Both wrong**, and each came from a single observation treated as decisive.

An edit reaches the agents after a delay. Marker string in a definition, spawned agents asked whether they had it, file reads forbidden:

```
~1 min after the edit    absent
~2.5 min                 absent
~6 min                   present
```

Nothing changed between the second and third — no edit, no commit, no restart. That disposes of both earlier theories, and the rows that produced them are instructive: a marker read PRESENT shortly after being **deleted from disk** (reads as proof the source is `HEAD`; was a stale copy), and a marker read PRESENT just after a commit (reads as proof committing publishes; the commit fell five minutes after the edit).

**So the guidance is a check, not a duration.** "Wait a few minutes" was the first draft and does not survive its own numbers — two of three observations sit inside what that phrase ordinarily means, and the 2.5-to-6 band was never probed. Put a m

## What was wrong

The probe checked that `chromium.executablePath()` names a file that exists. **That file is the full Chromium; a headless `launch()` opens the `chrome-headless-shell` beside it.** So it checked a binary no review in this repository ever opens — a guard reading a nearby declaration rather than the behaviour it is asked about, which root `AGENTS.md` names directly under *Code Review Rules*.

## Measured

Built with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` and symlinks; the real browser cache was never modified.

| | both installed | full only | shell only | neither |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `existsSync(executablePath)` | present | present | MISSING | MISSING |
| `launch()` | ok | UNUSABLE | ok | UNUSABLE |

The file check observes one of the two binaries, so it splits four configurations two ways and disagrees wherever the groupings cross.

**`shell only` is the dangerous column and is not hypothetical** — `playwright install --only-shell` is what Playwright suggests for CI images. There the old probe reported MISSING and sent the review to source **on a machine that renders every viewport**. That is the incident the paragraph above the probe already memorialises, recurring through the probe written to replace it.

## What was wrong

`.github/dependabot.yml` matched no pattern in `detect_changed_surfaces.py`, so a change touching only it classified as `unknown` — and `unknown` force-falls-back to the full runtime recommendation. The routing was right **by accident**, and indistinguishable from an oversight. That is how #253 was found.

## Behaviour does not change

Measured, not assumed: recommended targets for `.github/dependabot.yml` and for an unrecognised path are identical lists, and `unknown` is the only flag that moves. `verifier` confirmed the same by diffing the module against a copy with the entry deleted, across four file sets.

Nothing in `ci.yml` gates on `unknown` either — it is exported as a job output and read by no `if:`.

What changes is what the flag *means*. `unknown` is the catch-all for paths nobody has classified, and every known file leaning on it makes the flag harder to tighten later without silently reclassifying whatever else was sheltering there.

- It is the same class of repository metadata as `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**`, all already runtime **by explicit pattern**, not by fallback.

chore(web): load the vitest config the way Vite is going to load it

## Two blockers, and the second only appeared once the first was gone

Every `make test-web` run warned the config uses features unsupported by `configLoader: 'native'`, which is planned to become Vite's default — at which point the config stops loading rather than warning.

The issue proposed renaming to `.mts`. That clears the ESM-loaded-as-CommonJS complaint and reveals a second warning from the same check: `` `__dirname` (vitest.config.mts:17:25). Use `import.meta.dirname` instead ``.

Measured warning count:

| state | warnings |
| --- | --- |
| before | 1 |
| after the rename alone | **1** |
| after rename + `import.meta.dirname` | 0 |

So the suggested fix on its own would have left the deprecation in place while looking handled.

## Nothing is broken today

Vite still bundles this file and defines **both** `__dirname` and `import.meta.dirname` in that mode, so this is forward compatibility rather than a fix for a live failure. The comment says that, after review caught it claiming the file was "now read by" the native loader — which is not true yet.

## Why the Python guard is in the same commit

`tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py` read `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` by hardcoded name to assert vitest excludes the Playwright specs. The rename turns that into `FileNotFoundError` — a stack trace about a missing path rather than a statement about the exclu
===== #292
fix(ci): version eslint-config-next with next, not with eslint
Fixes #252.

## What was wrong

`eslint-config-next` is published from the Next.js repository and carries Next's version numbers — but `eslint-*` in the `eslint` group matched it by name and claimed it, because a dependency joins the **first** group whose patterns match and `eslint` is declared first.

So it inherited a family's blockers instead of its own. While the ESLint 10 major was held (three packages peer-cap ESLint below 10, so npm cannot install it), #223 bundled the two into one unmergeable pull request and `main` sat with `next` at 16.3.0 against `eslint-config-next` 16.2.12.

## Both halves are load bearing

Not redundant, and the guard proves it by mutation:

- **Exclude alone** → the package matches no later group until `npm-minor-patch`'s `"*"`, so it *detaches* from `next` rather than joining it.
- **`next` pattern alone** → `eslint` is declared first and still claims it.

## The guard

`tests/scripts/test_dependabot_groups.py` asserts group **membership**, computed from the config's own patterns — not the presence of the lines that produce it. Those come apart in both directions: an `exclude-patterns` entry can be dropped while the pattern below it stays, and a new group matching `eslint-*` can be declared above `next` and take the package back without either existing line changing. Grepping for either line reads as correct in both cases.

## What this is really about

#277 was filed as a cosmetic overlap — Next's dev-tools indicator covering the chat message input at 390x844, where the panel is a full-width sheet. The reason to take it is keyboard behaviour.

The indicator is a **focusable element positioned after the chat widget in the document**, so a dev server disagreed with production about the behaviour `chat.tsx` was most deliberately designed for. Measured at 1440x900 with the panel open, tabbing forward from the message input:

```
indicator on                     indicator off
1. Send message     dialog=1     1. Send message  dialog=1
2. Close chat       dialog=1     2. Close chat    dialog=1
3. NEXTJS-PORTAL    dialog=0     3. BODY          dialog=1
                                 4. #name         dialog=0
```

`chat.tsx` argues at length that Tab forward off the launcher should leave the page entirely, fire no `focusin`, and leave the panel **up** — closing it for the browser's address bar would be closing it for something that is not a page interaction. The indicator *is* a page interaction, so the panel closed a keystroke early.

`ui-review` reproduced the right-hand column independently against a dev server running this change, `#name` included, and confirmed the input is unobstructed at 390x844.

`eslint-config-next` is published from the Next.js repository and carries Next's version numbers — but `eslint-*` in the `eslint` group matched it by name and claimed it, because a dependency joins the **first** group whose patterns match and `eslint` is declared first.

`tests/scripts/test_dependabot_groups.py` asserts group **membership**, computed from the config's own patterns — not the presence of the lines that produce it. Those come apart in both directions: an `exclude-patterns` entry can be dropped while the pattern below it stays, and a new group matching `eslint-*` can be declared above `next` and take the package back without either existing line changing. Grepping for either line reads as correct in both cases.

2	
3	Web app scope for coding agents. This file adds authoritative instructions for
4	`apps/web/`; apply it together with the repo-root `AGENTS.md`. Put instructions
5	here, never in `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` or `apps/web/GEMINI.md`.
6	
7	## Entry points
8	
9	- Routes: `src/app/`
10	- UI components: `src/components/`
11	- Domain and API clients: `src/lib/`
12	- Route tests: `src/app/**/*.test.tsx` and `src/app/**/*.test.ts`
13	
14	## Local commands
15	
16	From repository root:
17	
18	```bash
19	make bootstrap
20	make agent-doctor
21	make dev-web
22	make lint
23	make typecheck
24	make test-web
25	npm run bootstrap
26	npm run doctor
27	npm run dev:web
28	npm run ci:web
29	```
30	
31	From the web app directory:
32	
33	```bash
34	make help
35	make setup
36	make dev
37	make quick-ci
38	make ci
39	```
40	
41	## Chat integration touchpoints
42	
43	- Web proxy route: `src/app/api/chat/service/route.ts`
44	- Web chat client: `src/lib/messaging.ts`
45	
46	When changing a request or response shape, update the chat service and its tests
47	in `services/chat/` as part of the same change.
48	
49	## Database access
50	
51	Prisma 7 removed `url` from the schema's `datasource` block. The connection URL
52	now lives in two places, both reading `DATABASE_URL`:
53	
54	- `prisma.config.ts` — used by `prisma migrate` and `prisma db seed`.
55	- A `PrismaPg` driver adapter passed to every `PrismaClient` constructor
56	  (`src/lib/prisma.ts` and `prisma/seed.ts`). Constructing `PrismaClient`
57	  without an adapter fails at runtime.
58	
59	The production image builds with `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1`, so anything Next
60	prerenders at build time captures the no-database response permanently. Route
61	handlers that read the database must opt out of static prerendering.
62	
63	## Code Review Rules
64	
65	- A route that reads the database must remain dynamic under the production
66	  `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1` build. Flag a change that can bake a build-time empty or
67	  fallback response into the deployed route instead of evaluating it at request time.
68	- Treat the web proxy, `src/lib/messaging.ts`, and the FastAPI request/response
69	  models as one contract. A payload change is incomplete unless both surfaces and
70	  their contract tests agree, including error and degraded responses.
71	- For UI changes, review the rendered behavior rather than class names alone.
72	  Preserve keyboard/focus semantics and responsive states; when `srcset` or source
73	  dimensions change, require evidence at representative 1x and 2x densities.
74	
75	## JavaScript, TypeScript, and React conventions
76	
77	- Prefer functions, plain objects, and ES module boundaries when no instance identity
78	  or lifecycle is required. Plain objects are mutable; never mutate React state, and
79	  use a class when an external API or a test double genuinely requires one.
80	- Avoid `any` and unchecked type assertions at application boundaries. Accept
81	  `unknown`, validate or narrow it, and keep unavoidable assertions local with a
82	  reason the compiler cannot establish the type itself.
83	- Prefer non-mutating collection operations. `sort()` mutates; use `toSorted()` when
84	  supported or sort a deliberate copy such as `[...items].sort(...)`.
85	- Keep rendering pure and use functional components and Hooks. Effects synchronize
86	  with external systems; derive values during render or update them in event handlers
87	  when no external synchronization is involved. Clean up subscriptions and include
88	  the dependencies the effect reads.
89	- Do not assume React Compiler is enabled. Check the current Next configuration before
90	  relying on compiler memoization, and add `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `React.memo`
91	  only when referential identity or measured performance makes it necessary.
92	- Keep environment access centralized, avoid service URLs in components, and prefer
93	  focused tests beside changed routes, components, and library modules.

`apps/web/`; apply it together with the repo-root `AGENTS.md`. Put instructions
here, never in `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` or `apps/web/GEMINI.md`.

## Entry points

- Routes: `src/app/`
- UI components: `src/components/`
- Domain and API clients: `src/lib/`
- Route tests: `src/app/**/*.test.tsx` and `src/app/**/*.test.ts`

## Local commands

From repository root:

```bash
make bootstrap
make agent-doctor
make dev-web
make lint
make typecheck
make test-web
npm run bootstrap
npm run doctor
npm run dev:web
npm run ci:web
```

From the web app directory:

```bash
make help
make setup
make dev
make quick-ci
make ci
```

## Chat integration touchpoints

- Web proxy route: `src/app/api/chat/service/route.ts`
- Web chat client: `src/lib/messaging.ts`

When changing a request or response shape, update the chat service and its tests
in `services/chat/` as part of the same change.

## Database access

Prisma 7 removed `url` from the schema's `datasource` block. The connection URL
now lives in two places, both reading `DATABASE_URL`:

- `prisma.config.ts` — used by `prisma migrate` and `prisma db seed`.
- A `PrismaPg` driver adapter passed to every `PrismaClient` constructor
  (`src/lib/prisma.ts` and `prisma/seed.ts`). Constructing `PrismaClient`
  without an adapter fails at runtime.

The production image builds with `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1`, so anything Next
prerenders at build time captures the no-database response permanently. Route
handlers that read the database must opt out of static prerendering.

## Code Review Rules

- A route that reads the database must remain dynamic under the production
  `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1` build. Flag a change that can bake a build-time empty or
  fallback response into the deployed route instead of evaluating it at request time.
- Treat the web proxy, `src/lib/messaging.ts`, and the FastAPI request/response
  models as one contract. A payload change is incomplete unless both surfaces and
  their contract tests agree, including error and degraded responses.
- For UI changes, review the rendered behavior rather than class names alone.
  Preserve keyboard/focus semantics and responsive states; when `srcset` or source
  dimensions change, require evidence at representative 1x and 2x densities.

## JavaScript, TypeScript, and React conventions

- Prefer functions, plain objects, and ES module boundaries when no instance identity
  or lifecycle is required. Plain objects are mutable; never mutate React state, and
  use a class when an external API or a test double genuinely requires one.
- Avoid `any` and unchecked type assertions at application boundaries. Accept
  `unknown`, validate or narrow it, and keep unavoidable assertions local with a
  reason the compiler cannot establish the type itself.
- Prefer non-mutating collection operations. `sort()` mutates; use `toSorted()` when
  supported or sort a deliberate copy such as `[...items].sort(...)`.
- Keep rendering pure and use functional components and Hooks. Effects synchronize
  with external systems; derive values during render or update them in event handlers
  when no external synchronization is involved. Clean up subscriptions and include
  the dependencies the effect reads.
- Do not assume React Compiler is enabled. Check the current Next configuration before
  relying on compiler memoization, and add `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `React.memo`
  only when referential identity or measured performance makes it necessary.
- Keep environment access centralized, avoid service URLs in components, and prefer
  focused tests beside changed routes, components, and library modules.

        `FileNotFoundError` -- a stack trace about a missing path, rather than

        exactly the set vitest will load: no sibling -- an editor backup, an

        # and against two configs would pass on whichever came first while

# AGENTS (Script Guardrails)

Root script-test scope for coding agents. This file adds authoritative
instructions for `tests/scripts/`; apply it together with the repo-root
`AGENTS.md`. Put instructions here, never in the sibling pointer files.

## Local commands

Run from the repository root:

```bash
make test-scripts
.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.scripts.<module> -v
```

## Code Review Rules

- Point a guard demonstration at a fixture tree, never the checkout it protects.
  Rebind every imported path constant the assertion dereferences; changing a root
  after derived constants were created does not redirect those constants.
- Prove that the intended assertion catches its named mistake, and separately prove
  the fixture was opened. A vacuity failure on an empty or mistyped path is not
  evidence that the behavioral assertion ran.
- Compare effective sets and outputs from the owning tool where practical. Parsing
  one declaration is insufficient when includes, excludes, defaults, comments, or
  other configuration can change what the compiler, runner, or hook actually uses.

## Fixture isolation

These modules compute path constants at import, so read the module and rebind every
constant the demonstrated assertion reaches:

- `test_image_encoding.py` reaches its files through `IMAGES_DIR`.
- `test_image_references.py` also needs `PUBLIC_DIR`, which `relative_to` depends on,
  and `REPO_ROOT`, which it walks for references.
- `test_page_headings.py` reads `REPO_ROOT` directly for component-supplied headings,
  so rebinding `APP_DIR` alone leaves that assertion pointed at the checkout.
- `test_published_ports.py` needs both `REPO_ROOT`, which `read()` resolves every
  coupled file through, and `COMPOSE`, which the port parser opens directly.

input.content:
Found while investigating #283, which asked whether the fix for that flake was a longer timeout or making `src/app/page.test.tsx` render less. Measuring where its ~2s actually goes says neither describes the cost: **it is the query, not the render.**

## Measured

Instrumented copy of `src/app/page.test.tsx`, idle 24-core machine, `performance.now()` around each step:

```
read categories.json      3ms
await Home()              5ms
render(tree)            120ms
getByRole('link', …)    793ms
render again             63ms
getByRole again         847ms
```

So the whole DOM the test builds costs 120ms, and one accessible-name query over it costs six to seven times that. Two `getByRole` calls would cost more than the page they inspect.

`getByRole` with a `name` resolves the role of every element in the document and computes an accessible name for each candidate, and jsdom's `getComputedStyle` is what makes that expensive. It scales with the document, not with the element being asserted on.

## A cheaper form asserts the same property

```
getByRole('link', { name })                    851ms
located element + toHaveAccessibleName(name)     9ms
```

input.content:
Fixes #283.

The suite ran on vitest's implicit 5000ms, which nobody chose. This states a budget and a flake policy, and adds a guard that reads both back from the runner.

## The decision #283 left open, settled by measurement

The issue offered two options: a longer timeout, or making `src/app/page.test.tsx` render less. Instrumenting the test says the second one is aimed at the wrong cost — the DOM it builds is 120ms of a ~2000ms test:

```
read categories.json      3ms
await Home()              5ms
render(tree)            120ms
getByRole('link', …)    793ms
```

More decisive: **page.test.tsx is only the first test to cross the line, not the only one within reach of it.** On an idle 24-core machine it runs 1.6–2.0s and nine others sit between 0.6s and 1.2s — `src/lib/user.test.ts` at 1189ms is real bcrypt work. The failing run in #283 was roughly 4–5x slower per test than an idle one, which is exactly where a 1189ms test also crosses 5000ms, and #283 recorded **two** files failing with only one identified. Speeding up one test hands the same flake to the next one.

So the fix is the budget, and the query cost is filed separately as #302 — where a located-element assertion measured 9ms against `getByRole`'s 851ms while still catching the defect the test exists for. Both are worth doing; neither substitutes for the other.

## Reproduced, then fixed

Synthetic CPU load, full suite, base config:

```
Test timed out in 5000ms.
 × src/app/page.test.tsx > Home page > names a product card once 6200ms
   reported at page.test.tsx:21, the `it(...)` line
```

That is the failure in #283, including the misleading line number. With `testTimeout: 20_000` at comparable load the same suite passes 159/159 across repeated runs, with the home page test between 1.6s and 3.9s.

## Honest limit of this fix

At an extreme synthetic load — around 4-5x oversubscription, `tests` reporting 204s against an idle 20s — one run had a single test cross 20s as well. A repeat at the same load passed everything, and I could not name the test from the reporter output before it went green again. **No fixed budget is proof against unbounded load.** What this changes is the multiplier: from under 3x of the slowest test's idle cost to about 10x. #302 is the other lever.

## Why 20s does not hide a slow test

The reporter prints a duration for any test over `slowTestThreshold` (300ms by default), so the six tests above that stay visible in every run's output regardless of the timeout. The signal #283 worried about losing is attached to the threshold, not to the budget.

## The guard reads the runner, not the config file

`src/test/runner-budget.test.ts` asserts on `task.timeout` and `task.retry` — the values the runner resolved for the test it is running. A regex over `vitest.config.mts` would assert that a line is written in a file, and those come apart in the case worth catching: a config vitest fails to load leaves the implicit 5000ms in force with the declaration still sitting there, which is not hypothetical for this file (#281 moved it between three loading modes). Demonstrated by mutating the config:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `testTimeout` line deleted | budget assertion fails, reporting 5000 |
| `testTimeout: 10_000` | budget assertion fails, reporting 10000 — a floor, not a presence check |
| `retry: 2` | retries assertion fails, and the runner retried the guard 3x, which is the setting proving itself |
| `retry: { count: 2 }` | retries assertion fails — the object form is normalised |
| `retry: { delay: 10 }` | both pass, correctly: `count` defaults to 0, confirmed by forcing a failure and counting one attempt, against four for `{ count: 3 }` |

The `retries nothing` assertion had no red phase, since retries are already off by default — the mutations above are what demonstrate it is not vacuous.

**What nothing here catches**, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: a per-file or per-test override (`it(..., 100)`, `describe.configure`), which is local by design; `hookTimeout`, a separate 10s budget left at its default because every hook in this suite is mock setup rather than work; and load beyond the budget, per the limit above.

## Notes

- `retry: 0` is vitest's default. Stated anyway, so that turning it on is a visible decision — the same thing `playwright.config.ts` does for the journeys, where `retries: 0` is explicit and guarded by `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py`.
- The policy lives in the config comment and its guard rather than in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, following how the journeys' identical policy is already recorded.

Fixes #283.

The suite ran on vitest's implicit 5000ms, which nobody chose. This states a budget and a flake policy, and adds a guard that reads both back from the runner.

## The decision #283 left open, settled by measurement

The issue offered two options: a longer timeout, or making `src/app/page.test.tsx` render less. Instrumenting the test says the second one is aimed at the wrong cost — the DOM it builds is 120ms of a ~2000ms test:

```
read categories.json      3ms
await Home()              5ms
render(tree)            120ms
getByRole('link', …)    793ms
```

More decisive: **page.test.tsx is only the first test to cross the line, not the only one within reach of it.** On an idle 24-core machine it runs 1.6–2.0s and nine others sit between 0.6s and 1.2s — `src/lib/user.test.ts` at 1189ms is real bcrypt work. The failing run in #283 was roughly 4–5x slower per test than an idle one, which is exactly where a 1189ms test also crosses 5000ms, and #283 recorded **two** files failing with only one identified. Speeding up one test hands the same flake to the next one.

So the fix is the budget, and the query cost is filed separately as #302 — where a located-element assertion measured 9ms against `getByRole`'s 851ms while still catching the defect the test exists for. Both are worth doing; neither substitutes for the other.

## Reproduced, then fixed

Synthetic CPU load, full suite, base config:

```
Test timed out in 5000ms.
 × src/app/page.test.tsx > Home page > names a product card once 6200ms
   reported at page.test.tsx:21, the `it(...)` line
```

That is the failure in #283, including the misleading line number. With `testTimeout: 20_000` at comparable load the same suite passes 159/159 across repeated runs, with the home page test between 1.6s and 3.9s.

## Honest limit of this fix

At an extreme synthetic load — around 4-5x oversubscription, `tests` reporting 204s against an idle 20s — one run had a single test cross 20s as well. A repeat at the same load passed everything, and I could not name the test from the reporter output before it went green again. **No fixed budget is proof against unbounded load.** What this changes is the multiplier: from under 3x of the slowest test's idle cost to about 10x. #302 is the other lever.

## Why 20s does not hide a slow test

The reporter prints a duration for any test over `slowTestThreshold` (300ms by default), so the six tests above that stay visible in every run's output regardless of the timeout. The signal #283 worried about losing is attached to the threshold, not to the budget.

## The guard reads the runner, not the config file

`src/test/runner-budget.test.ts` asserts on `task.timeout` and `task.retry` — the values the runner resolved for the test it is running. A regex over `vitest.config.mts` would assert that a line is written in a file, and those come apart in the case worth catching: a config vitest fails to load leaves the implicit 5000ms in force with the declaration still sitting there, which is not hypothetical for this file (#281 moved it between three loading modes). Demonstrated by mutating the config:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `testTimeout` line deleted | budget assertion fails, reporting 5000 |
| `testTimeout: 10_000` | budget assertion fails, reporting 10000 — a floor, not a presence check |
| `retry: 2` | retries assertion fails, and the runner retried the guard 3x, which is the setting proving itself |
| `retry: { count: 2 }` | retries assertion fails — the object form is normalised |
| `retry: { delay: 10 }` | both pass, correctly: `count` defaults to 0, confirmed by forcing a failure and counting one attempt, against four for `{ count: 3 }` |

The `retries nothing` assertion had no red phase, since retries are already off by default — the mutations above are what demonstrate it is not vacuous.

**What nothing here catches**, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: a per-file or per-test override (`it(..., 100)`, `describe.configure`), which is local by design; `hookTimeout`, a separate 10s budget left at its default because every hook in this suite is mock setup rather than work; and load beyond the budget, per the limit above.

## Notes

- `retry: 0` is vitest's default. Stated anyway, so that turning it on is a visible decision — the same thing `playwright.config.ts` does for the journeys, where `retries: 0` is explicit and guarded by `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py`.
- The policy lives in the config comment and its guard rather than in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, following how the journeys' identical policy is already recorded.
- `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py` reads this config to assert the `e2e/**` exclusion, so `make test-scripts` is coupled to this diff even though no script changed. It was run.

Fixes #283.

The suite ran on vitest's implicit 5000ms, which nobody chose. This states a budget and a flake policy, and adds a guard that reads both back from the runner.

## The decision #283 left open, settled by measurement

The issue offered two options: a longer timeout, or making `src/app/page.test.tsx` render less. Instrumenting the test says the second one is aimed at the wrong cost — the DOM it builds is 120ms of a ~2000ms test:

```
read categories.json      3ms
await Home()              5ms
render(tree)            120ms
getByRole('link', …)    793ms
```

More decisive: **page.test.tsx is only the first test to cross the line, not the only one within reach of it.** On an idle 24-core machine it runs 1.6–2.0s and nine others sit between 0.6s and 1.2s — `src/lib/user.test.ts` at 1189ms is real bcrypt work. The failing run in #283 was roughly 4–5x slower per test than an idle one, which is exactly where a 1189ms test also crosses 5000ms, and #283 recorded **two** files failing with only one identified. Speeding up one test hands the same flake to the next one.

So the fix is the budget, and the query cost is filed separately as #302 — where a located-element assertion measured 9ms against `getByRole`'s 851ms while still catching the defect the test exists for. Both are worth doing; neither substitutes for the other.

## Reproduced, then fixed

Synthetic CPU load, full suite, base config:

```
Test timed out in 5000ms.
 × src/app/page.test.tsx > Home page > names a product card once 6200ms
   reported at page.test.tsx:21, the `it(...)` line
```

That is the failure in #283, including the misleading line number. With `testTimeout: 20_000` at comparable load the same suite passes 159/159 across repeated runs, with the home page test between 1.6s and 3.9s.

## Honest limit of this fix

At an extreme synthetic load — around 4-5x oversubscription, `tests` reporting 204s against an idle 20s — one run had a single test cross 20s as well. A repeat at the same load passed everything, and I could not name the test from the reporter output before it went green again. **No fixed budget is proof against unbounded load.** What this changes is the multiplier: from under 3x of the slowest test's idle cost to about 10x. #302 is the other lever.

## Why 20s does not hide a slow test

The reporter prints a duration for any test over `slowTestThreshold` (300ms by default), so every test above that stays visible in each run's output regardless of the timeout. The signal #283 worried about losing is attached to the threshold, not to the budget.

## The guard reads the runner, not the config file

`src/test/runner-budget.test.ts` asserts on `task.timeout` and `task.retry` — the values the runner resolved for the test it is running. A regex over `vitest.config.mts` would assert that a line is written in a file, and those come apart in the case worth catching: a config vitest fails to load leaves the implicit 5000ms in force with the declaration still sitting there, which is not hypothetical for this file (#281 moved it between three loading modes). Demonstrated by mutating the config:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `testTimeout` line deleted | budget assertion fails, reporting 5000 |
| `testTimeout: 10_000` | budget assertion fails, reporting 10000 — a floor, not a presence check |
| `retry: 2` | retries assertion fails, and the runner retried the guard 3x, which is the setting proving itself |
| `retry: { count: 2 }` | retries assertion fails — the object form is normalised |
| `retry: { delay: 10 }` | both pass, correctly: `count` defaults to 0, confirmed by forcing a failure and counting one attempt, against four for `{ count: 3 }` |

The `retries nothing` assertion had no red phase, since retries are already off by default — the mutations above are what demonstrate it is not vacuous.

**What nothing here catches**, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: a per-file or per-test override (`it(..., 100)`, `describe.configure`), which is local by design; `hookTimeout`, a separate 10s budget left at its default because every hook in this suite is mock setup rather than work; and load beyond the budget, per the limit above.

## Notes

- `retry: 0` is vitest's default. Stated anyway, so that turning it on is a visible decision — the same thing `playwright.config.ts` does for the journeys, where `retries: 0` is explicit and guarded by `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py`.
- The policy lives in the config comment and its guard rather than in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, following how the journeys' identical policy is already recorded.
- `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py` reads this config to assert the `e2e/**` exclusion, so `make test-scripts` is coupled to this diff even though no script changed. It was run.

Found by `code-review` during #283, which added a vitest-side flake guard that reads the resolved value from the runner. That made the journey side the weaker half of the pair.

## What is wrong

`tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py::test_retries_are_not_enabled` asserts on the *text* of `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`:

```python
config = read("apps/web/playwright.config.ts")
self.assertRegex(config, re.compile(r"retries:\s*0"))
```

That is a declaration read, not a measurement. It passes while retries are on if `retries: 0` appears anywhere in the file — in a comment, in a dead object literal, in a `projects[]` entry that is not the live one — and the live value is `2`. It is the shape the root `AGENTS.md` *Code Review Rules* tell reviewers to reject: "Require guards to measure effective behavior, not a nearby declaration."

Nothing is wrong with the current value. `playwright.config.ts` does state `retries: 0` unconditionally today, with no `process.env.CI ? 2 : 0`. This is about what the guard would notice if that changed.

## What the equivalent measurement looks like

Playwright exposes the resolved value to a spec through `testInfo.project.retries`, so a journey can assert what the runner will actually do, the way `apps/web/src/test/runner-budget.test.ts` now does for vitest via `task.timeout` and `task.retry`:

```ts
test('the journeys do not retry', ({}, testInfo) => {
  expect(testInfo.project.retries).toBe(0)
})
```

Two things to weigh before doing that:

- A journey spec needs the composed stack to run, so this moves a check that currently costs milliseconds in `make test-scripts` into a suite that costs minutes and needs docker. A spec that asserts only on `testInfo` touches no page, but it still runs inside the run that needs the stack.
- The python guard also runs on machines that never build a stack, which is part of why it is where it is.

So the options are: replace the regex with a journey assertion, keep both (cheap declaration check plus effective check), or leave it and accept that the journey policy is guarded more weakly than the unit one. Worth a deliberate choice rather than the current implicit one.

## Also worth noting

`timeout: 30_000` and `expect: { timeout: 10_000 }` in the same file are guarded by nothing at all. If a runner-read check gets added, those are the same `testInfo.project`/`testInfo.timeout` read and cost nothing extra.

## Review

`code-review`: **no defects**, two refinements, both applied. It re-derived the evidence rather than taking the summary, including reading the vitest 4.1.10 runner source to confirm the guard measures the enforced value: `chunk-artifact.js` computes `options.timeout ?? runner.config.testTimeout`, stores it on the task, and passes *that variable* to `withTimeout`, and the runner's own `getRetryCount` normalises `retry` exactly as `retryCount()` here does.

Refinements applied:

1. The config comment said raising the budget "does" hide the slow-test signal, immediately before evidence that the signal is absent at any timeout — the comment stated the conclusion the rest of its own sentence refutes. This is the second time in this change that this comment overstated in one direction or the other; it now says the signal was never there.
2. The guard's *what nothing here catches* list recorded the `testTimeout` deletion case but not the `retry` one. Deleting `retry: 0` leaves both assertions green, because an unset `retry` also resolves to 0 — the asymmetry is that `testTimeout`'s fallback is a *different* number. Now written down.

It answered the three questions I asked and agreed with the calls: 20s is right and a floor is the right assertion shape, no `tests/scripts` regex guard should be added alongside a runner-read one, and the policy should not be restated in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`.

One finding outside this change, filed as **#303**: the journeys' no-retry policy is guarded by `re.search(r"retries:\s*0", config)` over the text of `playwright.config.ts`, which would pass on a `retries: 0` in a comment while the live value was 2. The reviewer noted one limit on its own work: it could not assess how the 20s budget behaves on CI runner hardware, since #283's failure is load-dependent and all measurements here are from one machine.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
Fixes #283.

The suite ran on vitest's implicit 5000ms, which nobody chose. This states a budget and a flake policy, and adds a guard that reads both back from the runner.

## The decision #283 left open, settled by measurement

The issue offered two options: a longer timeout, or making `src/app/page.test.tsx` render less. Instrumenting the test says the second one is aimed at the wrong cost — the DOM it builds is 120ms of a ~2000ms test:

```
read categories.json      3ms
await Home()              5ms
render(tree)            120ms
getByRole('link', …)    793ms
```

More decisive: **page.test.tsx is only the first test to cross the line, not the only one within reach of it.** On an idle 24-core machine it runs 1.6–2.0s and nine others sit between 0.6s and 1.2s — `src/lib/user.test.ts` at 1189ms is real bcrypt work. The failing run in #283 was roughly 4–5x slower per test than an idle one, which is exactly where a 1189ms test also crosses 5000ms, and #283 recorded **two** files failing with only one identified. Speeding up one test hands the same flake to the next one.

So the fix is the budget, and the query cost is filed separately as #302 — where a located-element assertion measured 9ms against `getByRole`'s 851ms while still catching the defect the test exists for. Both are worth doing; neither substitutes for the other.

## Reproduced, then fixed

Synthetic CPU load, full suite, base config:

```
Test timed out in 5000ms.
 × src/app/page.test.tsx > Home page > names a product card once 6200ms
   reported at page.test.tsx:21, the `it(...)` line
```

That is the failure in #283, including the misleading line number. With `testTimeout: 20_000` at comparable load the same suite passes 159/159 across repeated runs, with the home page test between 1.6s and 3.9s.

## Honest limit of this fix

At an extreme synthetic load — around 4-5x oversubscription, `tests` reporting 204s against an idle 20s — one run had a single test cross 20s as well. A repeat at the same load passed everything, and I could not name the test from the reporter output before it went green again. **No fixed budget is proof against unbounded load.** What this changes is the multiplier: from under 3x of the slowest test's idle cost to about 10x. #302 is the other lever.

## #283's other worry is real: this does hide slow tests

The issue said raising the timeout hides the signal that the test is slow. My first draft of the config comment claimed the opposite — that the reporter keeps printing durations over `slowTestThreshold` — and then I checked it:

```
$ npx vitest run          # what `npm test` runs
 Test Files  38 passed (38)
      Tests  159 passed (159)
```

No per-test output at all on a green run. The default reporter prints durations for failures only, so the 20 tests over 300ms were already invisible before this change and stay invisible after it, at any timeout. `vitest run --reporter=verbose` prints all 159, which is where every number in this PR came from.

So the honest position is that the budget buys headroom and costs nothing that was working — not that the signal survives. The signal was never in the default output. #302 carries the cost itself; the comment in the config now says this rather than the reverse.

## The guard reads the runner, not the config file

`src/test/runner-budget.test.ts` asserts on `task.timeout` and `task.retry` — the values the runner resolved for the test it is running. A regex over `vitest.config.mts` would assert that a line is written in a file, and those come apart in the case worth catching: a config vitest fails to load leaves the implicit 5000ms in force with the declaration still sitting there, which is not hypothetical for this file (#281 moved it between three loading modes). Demonstrated by mutating the config:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `testTimeout` line deleted | budget assertion fails, reporting 5000 |
| `testTimeout: 10_000` | budget assertion fails, reporting 10000 — a floor, not a presence check |
| `retry: 2` | retries assertion fails, and the runner retried the guard 3x, which is the setting proving itself |
| `retry: { count: 2 }` | retries assertion fails — the object form is normalised |
| `retry: { delay: 10 }` | both pass, correctly: `count` defaults to 0, confirmed by forcing a failure and counting one attempt, against four for `{ count: 3 }` |

The `retries nothing` assertion had no red phase, since retries are already off by default — the mutations above are what demonstrate it is not vacuous.

**What nothing here catches**, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: a per-file or per-test override (`it(..., 100)`, `describe.configure`), which is local by design; `hookTimeout`, a separate 10s budget left at its default because every hook in this suite is mock setup rather than work; and load beyond the budget, per the limit above.

## Notes

- `retry: 0` is vitest's default. Stated anyway, so that turning it on is a visible decision — the same thing `playwright.config.ts` does for the journeys, where `retries: 0` is explicit and guarded by `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py`.
- The policy lives in the config comment and its guard rather than in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, following how the journeys' identical policy is already recorded.
- `tests/scripts/test_e2e_journey_wiring.py` reads this config to assert the `e2e/**` exclusion, so `make test-scripts` is coupled to this diff even though no script changed. It was run.

It re-derived the evidence rather than taking the summary, including reading the vitest 4.1.10 runner source to confirm the guard measures the enforced value: `chunk-artifact.js` computes `options.timeout ?? runner.config.testTimeout`, stores it on the task, and passes *that variable* to `withTimeout`, and the runner's own `getRetryCount` normalises `retry` exactly as `retryCount()` here does.
+Refinements applied:

+1. The config comment said raising the budget "does" hide the slow-test signal, immediately before evidence that the signal is absent at any timeout — the comment stated the conclusion the rest of its own sentence refutes. This is the second time in this change that this comment overstated in one direction or the other; it now says the signal was never there.

+2. The guard's *what nothing here catches* list recorded the `testTimeout` deletion case but not the `retry` one. Deleting `retry: 0` leaves both assertions green, because an unset `retry` also resolves to 0 — the asymmetry is that `testTimeout`'s fallback is a *different* number. Now written down.

+It answered the three questions I asked and agreed with the calls: 20s is right and a floor is the right assertion shape, no `tests/scripts` regex guard should be added alongside a runner-read one, and the policy should not be restated in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`.

+One finding outside this change, filed as **#303**: the journeys' no-retry policy is guarded by `re.search(r"retries:\s*0", config)` over the text of `playwright.config.ts`, which would pass on a `retries: 0` in a comment while the live value was 2. That is the declaration-reading shape this repository's review rules reject, and this change makes the journey half the weaker one of the pair. `testInfo.project.retries` is the resolved value a journey could assert instead — I checked the type exists (`FullProject.retries: number`) rather than assuming the API.

+The reviewer noted one limit on its own work: it could not assess how the 20s budget behaves on CI runner hardware, since #283's failure is load-dependent and all measurements here are from one machine.

fix(web): give the vitest suite a chosen budget and a flake policy

The suite ran on vitest's implicit 5000ms, which nobody chose, and
`src/app/page.test.tsx` intermittently crossed it under machine load.
Reproduced under synthetic load against the old config: `Test timed out
in 5000ms`, 6200ms, reported at page.test.tsx:21 exactly as filed. At
comparable load the same suite passes 159/159 with the new budget.

#283 offered a second option -- make that test render less -- and the
measurement says it is aimed at the wrong cost. The DOM the test builds
is 120ms of its ~2000ms; one `getByRole` name query is 793ms. And the
test is only the first of ten within 5x of the old budget: the next is
`src/lib/user.test.ts` at 1189ms of real bcrypt work, which is very
likely #283's unidentified second failing file. Speeding up one test
moves the flake rather than removing it. The query cost is #302.

`retry: 0` is vitest's default, stated so that turning it on is a
visible decision, and for the reason `playwright.config.ts` gives for
the journeys: a retried failure is a failure that gets ignored. #283
exists because a real timeout went green on the next run, which is the
observation retries would have deleted.

The guard reads `task.timeout` and `task.retry` from the runner rather
than regexing the config, because a config vitest fails to load leaves
5000ms in force with the declaration still in the file -- not
hypothetical for this file, which #281 moved between loading modes.
Its floor was demonstrated by mutation: deleting `testTimeout` reports
5000, `testTimeout: 10_000` reports 10000, `retry: 2` and
`retry: { count: 2 }` both fail while `retry: { delay: 10 }` correctly
passes.

Two review refinements applied, no defects: the comment above
`testTimeout` had said raising the budget hides the slow-test signal,
which contradicted its own evidence -- the default reporter prints
nothing on a green run at any timeout, so the signal was never there --
